context.requirement_text:
Source: GH #2323 (ISS-1034, Q-1016): 'the process validator checks
that the referenced nodes exist and precede the node', AMENDED by BA
decision 2026-10-07: a named node may lie on a PARALLEL branch (no
path between the two nodes); strict precedence applies only when the
named node is on the same path as this node. Plus the
design-intent constraint that the REQ-455 validator WARNS (not a
violation) when distinct_from names a node that routes to the same
single-member role (the node could never complete). Adds checks
beside the existing node-attribute checks in
lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex and the install-time role warnings
added by REQ-455 (unbound task roles are reported as a warning list,
never an automatic binding).

BUILDS:
RESERVED CODES (copy exactly from REQ-459 design section 1.2; do
not invent others). Violations: `:invalid_distinct_from`,
`:distinct_from_on_non_human_task`, `:distinct_from_self_reference`,
`:distinct_from_unknown_node`, `:distinct_from_not_human_task`,
`:distinct_from_downstream_only`. Warning (string prefix, not an
atom): `distinct_from_single_member_role:`. They extend
Graph.Violation.code(); checks are CHK-26 (check_distinct_from/1,
checks 1 and 2) and CHK-27 (check_distinct_from_position/1, check 3),
appended after CHK-25 in Graph.validate_node_attributes/1.

1. Shape: `distinct_from` on a HUMAN_TASK is a list of non-empty node
   ids without duplicates and without the node's own id; on any other
   node type it is a violation. Codes: :invalid_distinct_from (not a
   list, non-string or empty entry, duplicate),
   :distinct_from_on_non_human_task, :distinct_from_self_reference.
2. Existence: every listed id is a node of the same definition and a
   HUMAN_TASK; a missing id is a violation naming node and id
   (:distinct_from_unknown_node); an existing node that is not a
   HUMAN_TASK is :distinct_from_not_human_task.
3. Path position: a listed node must not be reachable only AFTER this
   node (this node has a path to it and it has no path to this node):
   a node downstream-only is a violation naming both, since it can
   never have completed when this node is checked
   (:distinct_from_downstream_only). A listed node that precedes this
   node, is on a parallel or mutually exclusive branch (no path
   either way) or is on a rework loop (a path both ways) passes
   (design section 1.5 relation table). Consequence: three parallel
   nodes may each name the other two; a node and its own downstream
   successor may not name each other (l1-approval naming l2-approval
   fails). A node unreachable from START passes (CHK-22 reports it).
4. Same-role WARNING: when this node and a listed node route to the
   same role (attributes["role"] only, not escalation_role) and that
   role has exactly one member in the installing tenant, the
   validation result carries a WARNING (not a violation, prefix
   `distinct_from_single_member_role:`) naming both nodes and the
   role, because the single member could never complete the second
   node. One warning per unordered pair (ids sorted); it applies to
   preceding, parallel and loop pairs alike; zero members is the
   unbound_task_role: case, not this one. Evaluated where tenant role
   membership is known: pack install and
   Definitions.validate_definition_graph/2 (which already holds the
   tenant prefix), NOT in the activate response (record-shaped,
   carries no warnings) and not at pure Graph validation without a
   tenant. New RoleBinding functions single_member_pairs/1,
   member_counts/2 (one prefix-scoped query over group_members and
   tenant_role, returns counts only, run only when a definition has
   a candidate pair) and format_single_member_warning/2; the warning
   is the third source of ValidationWarnings.for_definitions/2
   (created by REQ-461). Members are counted as distinct
   group_members.user_id of the role's bound group regardless of
   users.status (design OQ-2).
requirement_acceptance_criteria: one test per check 1 to 3 with a minimal definition that violates only that check, asserting the code, the node id and the listed id; one passing neighbour per check

a distinct_from naming the node itself (:distinct_from_self_reference), a non-existent id (:distinct_from_unknown_node), a service-task id (:distinct_from_not_human_task), a duplicate (:invalid_distinct_from), and a node reachable only after this node (:distinct_from_downstream_only) are each reported (five negative tests); a non-list value is :invalid_distinct_from and the attribute on a non-HUMAN_TASK node is :distinct_from_on_non_human_task; each asserts the reserved code from the REQ-459 design section 1.2, no other code name

parallel branches: nodes P1, P2, P3 after a fork, each naming the other two, produce no violation; a listed node on the same path before this node passes; a listed node on a rework loop (path both ways) passes

check 4: a definition installed in a tenant where the shared role has one member returns a WARNING naming both nodes and the role, and the definition still installs (status unchanged); in a tenant where the role has two members no warning is returned

a distinct_from check never changes a definition (activation of a definition with only a warning succeeds, warnings never block); the distinct_from_single_member_role: warning appears in the pack-install `warnings` and the POST /definitions/:id/validate 200 body (not in the activate response)
every shipped definition is run through the validator in a test; for each, the count of new findings is quoted; shipped definitions without distinct_from report none
mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, scoped mix test over test/letflow/definitions, and mix letflow.check_boundaries pass, real output quoted

SECURITY-REVIEWER verdict recorded: check 4's member_counts/2 is a new query over group_members and tenant_role (the design confirms the condition is met); it is prefix-scoped (INV-1) and returns counts only, never user ids, names or emails (INV-2)

task.description:
STEP 02a - IMPLEMENT (ELIXIR-DEV). Implement REQ-464 exactly per the REQ-459 design. Read the full requirement text and acceptance criteria in this handoff's context, the design sections named below, docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, security-invariants.md and docs/anti-patterns.md (newest entries) first.

BUILD (production code only; TEST-DESIGNER writes the new tests at step 03):
1. lib/letflow/definitions/graph/violation.ex (or wherever Graph.Violation code() is defined; find it): extend the code type with EXACTLY :invalid_distinct_from, :distinct_from_on_non_human_task, :distinct_from_self_reference, :distinct_from_unknown_node, :distinct_from_not_human_task, :distinct_from_downstream_only. No other names.
2. lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex: CHK-26 check_distinct_from/1 (checks 1 and 2: shape + existence; violation naming node id and the offending listed id) and CHK-27 check_distinct_from_position/1 (check 3), appended after CHK-25 in validate_node_attributes/1. Check 3: listed node L, this node N: if N has a path to L and L has NO path to N => :distinct_from_downstream_only naming both; preceding (L->N only), parallel/mutually exclusive (no path either way) and loop (both ways) pass. A node unreachable from START passes (CHK-22 reports it). Reuse the existing reachability/transitive-closure helpers in graph.ex if any (read them; do not duplicate one). A non-HUMAN_TASK node carrying distinct_from => :distinct_from_on_non_human_task (key present, any value). Order of codes per node deterministic; do not emit position/existence violations for ids already flagged invalid/self/unknown/not-human-task (decide from design 1.2/1.5 and report).
3. lib/letflow/definitions/role_binding.ex (read the REQ-455 unbound_task_role warnings code first and mirror its prefix handling): single_member_pairs/1 (pure: from a graph/definition, the unordered node pairs [N, L] where N has a distinct_from listing L, both HUMAN_TASK, same attributes["role"] (NOT escalation_role), pairs deduplicated and ids sorted so a pair named both ways gives ONE entry; applies to preceding, parallel and loop pairs alike), member_counts/2 (ONE prefix-scoped query over group_members and tenant_role returning role=>count only, count of DISTINCT group_members.user_id of the role's bound group regardless of users.status (design OQ-2: do NOT join users); never user ids/names/emails; run ONLY when the definition has at least one candidate pair: zero candidate pairs => zero queries), format_single_member_warning/2 producing the string with prefix `distinct_from_single_member_role:` naming both nodes and the role (nothing about users). Exactly one member => warning; zero members is the existing unbound_task_role: case (no distinct_from warning); two or more => none.
4. lib/letflow/definitions/validation_warnings.ex (created by REQ-461; read it): the single-member warning is the THIRD source of Letflow.Definitions.ValidationWarnings.for_definitions/2. Wire it so it appears in pack-install `warnings` and the POST /definitions/:id/validate 200 body (via Definitions.validate_definition_graph/2 which holds the tenant prefix), NEVER in the activate response, and not at pure Graph validation without a tenant. Warnings never block install/activate (status unchanged).
5. Violations 1-3 surface wherever Graph.validate_node_attributes/1 runs (validate, create, update, import, pack install): verify by reading the call sites and by one real run through the validate path.
6. The requirement/design name RoleBinding.member_counts/2; the REVIEWER of REQ-461 preferred an Identity-owned counting function. FOLLOW the requirement/design (RoleBinding.member_counts/2) unless the code makes it wrong (e.g. a boundary violation reported by mix letflow.check_boundaries); report your finding either way (does RoleBinding already read group_members/tenant_role? what does the Identity context offer?).
7. Do NOT edit docs/requirements.yaml, docs/status, .claude/agents text, or add tests (TEST-DESIGNER's job), except to fix an EXISTING test or fixture that your change legitimately breaks (report each). Add @doc/@spec per project convention.

VERIFY (run and quote real output): git branch --show-current; `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`; `mix format --check-formatted`; `mix letflow.check_boundaries` (MIX_TEST_PARTITION unset). Then the CAUTION sweep:
 (a) grep the WHOLE test/ tree, test/fixtures and lib/ for `distinct_from` and list every hit; run each test FILE that builds a definition with distinct_from (at least test/letflow/engine_distinct_from_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/tasks_distinct_from_test.exs, test/letflow/engine_distinct_from_concurrency_test.exs, plus anything using test/support/sod_support.ex) as separate sequential invocations; report each Result: line. If a hand-built definition is now refused (non-existent node, downstream-only, etc.) FIX THE TEST FIXTURE (not the validator), say which, and explain why the fixture was not legit-by-design before.
 (b) run the existing validator/RoleBinding/ValidationWarnings neighbour tests: grep test/ for RoleBinding, unbound_task_role, ValidationWarnings, validate_node_attributes, validate_definition_graph and run each file found (separate invocations): at least test/letflow/definitions/required_outputs_shipped_definitions_test.exs, required_outputs_validation_test.exs, required_outputs_surfaces_test.exs and the role_binding tests. Tests asserting exact `warnings` lists may change only if a candidate pair exists; report any.
Result fields: summary, files_changed (git diff --stat), design_vs_requirement_differences, identity_counting_finding, neighbour_sweep (file -> Result), notes. COMMIT your production change yourself in ONE commit titled `feat(REQ-464/Q-1027): distinct_from validator checks CHK-26/CHK-27 and single-member-role warning [Q-1027 / GH #2342]` (explicit paths only) and quote the hash.
RUN CONSTRAINTS (every agent in this run):
- Branch feat/REQ-464-distinct-from-validator-Q-1027 (from origin/main 5b7b8c90). Verify with `git branch --show-current` first; STOP and report if different. Do NOT push, open a PR, merge, touch the letflow-queue (lock 1027 is held by tvolodi-orch), touch branch test/authz-deny-log-deterministic-capture, or the untracked letflow-3.code-workspace. Stage files by explicit path only; never git add -A / git add . . COMMIT your own production/test change (one commit) BEFORE returning, and quote the hash (mutation testers use git checkout; uncommitted work is unrecoverable and has destroyed work before).
- Design: lib/letflow/design/req459-required-outputs-and-distinct-person.md section 1 (1.1, 1.2 reserved codes, 1.5 relation table), the traceability table, 'Adjustments for REQ-460..466' for REQ-464, Open question OQ-2. Where the requirement text and the design differ on a detail the DESIGN WINS; list every difference in result.design_vs_requirement_differences.
- RAM is VERY tight (0.4-2 GB free; the harness KILLS runs at critical memory). mix commands strictly sequential, ONE BEAM at a time; before each mix test check free RAM: powershell -NoProfile -c "[math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,2)". Scoped single test FILES only (never a directory or the full suite). `export MIX_TEST_PARTITION=3` ONLY for tests (unset for tooling tasks like compile/format/check_*); use a unique number (e.g. 16) for files that mutate shared state. If a run is killed, report it and do NOT loop.
- Real Postgres only. Never report 'should pass'; quote real Result: lines.
- docs/anti-patterns.md newest entries: a validator that starts refusing at activate must be checked against EVERY test that activates hand-built definitions: grep the WHOLE test/ tree (and fixtures) for the attribute (distinct_from). REQ-463's tests (test/letflow/engine_distinct_from_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/tasks_distinct_from_test.exs, test/letflow/engine_distinct_from_concurrency_test.exs, test/support/sod_support.ex and any other hit) build definitions with distinct_from and activate/create them: run each as a separate invocation and FIX THE TEST FIXTURES (never weaken the validator) if a legit-by-design definition is now refused; say which.
- Commit titles: feat|fix|test|docs(REQ-464/Q-1027): ... [Q-1027 / GH #2342], ending with the trailer line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not commit handoff-file edits unless this handoff says so: ORCH commits them.
- Claim the handoff by setting top-level status to IN_PROGRESS only; at the end set status COMPLETED (or FAILED) and fill result (summary, verdict PASS/FAIL, issues, artifacts_out, evidence with quoted real output, next_action). Do not touch started_at/created_at. Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log. If you rewrite the handoff JSON with PowerShell strip any UTF-8 BOM (lint_handoffs rejects it); prefer python json.dump with encoding utf-8.
- Scratch files go in the scratchpad dir C:\Users\tvolo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-tvolo-dev-ai-dala-letflow-3\def1f47a-501c-4830-b7ce-a68038cf3791\scratchpad\r464\ (never in the repo, never /tmp).
